4540.title: [UWP] Add modern .NET UWP views and native integration
4540.body:
[UWP] Add modern .NET UWP views and native integration (#4540)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/2746
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5155
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4540#issuecomment-5124287682
Context: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/4540#issuecomment-5158712361

Support the in-box Windows.UI.Xaml stack on modern .NET by sharing the
WinUI rendering implementation while retaining platform-specific package,
WinRT component and ANGLE build identities. Reuse the Win32 Skia and
HarfBuzz binaries rather than introducing another core native build.

~~ Modern UWP public programming model ~~

Add SkiaSharp.Views.UWP for net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0, with a declared
minimum Windows version of 10.0.17763.0. This supports modern .NET UWP;
it does not restore the legacy uap10.0 target reported in #2746.

Expose SKXamlCanvas for CPU drawing, SKSwapChainPanel for ANGLE-backed
GPU drawing, AngleSwapChainPanel, UWPExtensions and the corresponding
PaintSurface event arguments in SkiaSharp.Views.UWP. Drawing callbacks
receive control-managed surfaces; the CPU surface is disposed after the
callback, while GPU resources are released when the context is destroyed.

Use SkiaSharp.Views.UWP as the assembly identity, distinct from WinUI's
SkiaSharp.Views.Windows. SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.UWP supplies the UWP ANGLE
libraries, native helper and managed projection for win-x86, win-x64 and
win-arm64, not a new libSkiaSharp or libHarfBuzzSharp. Reactivate its
previously obsolete package ID, register the Views package, and include the
UWP assemblies in signing, version tracking and the Windows solutions.
The sample exercises this combination; that is not Store-certification
evidence for the declared OS and architecture range.

~~ Share implementation without changing WinRT platform identities ~~

Move the WinUI controls and EGL context sources to
SkiaSharp.Views.WinRT.Shared, compiled by the UWP and WinUI project heads.
Select Microsoft.UI.Xaml and DispatcherQueue for WinUI, and
Windows.UI.Xaml and CoreDispatcher for UWP. The UWP UI-thread render loop
uses its completion source to wait for the dispatched frame.

Move BufferExtensions and PropertySetExtensions from the WinUI native
project into SkiaSharp.Views.WinRT.Native.Shared. Retain separate IDL,
PCH, project and projection heads: UWP uses its own runtime-class namespace
and AppContainer/WindowsApp.lib contract; WinUI retains its desktop and
Windows App SDK contract. NativeNamespace.h rejects missing or conflicting
platform defines. Buffer access still uses IBufferByteAccess, and the
PropertySet helpers still insert explicitly typed WinRT property values.
Include the shared native sources in both cache dependency sets.

Preserve WindowsExtensions for the Windows WinUI build by testing
WINUI && WINDOWS. Testing WINUI alone would rename the UWPExtensions
class consumed by non-Windows Uno builds, which also define WINUI.
Update Uno's source link and document the compilation-symbol boundary.
The pointer-based GLES/EGL prerequisite from #5155 is already in the base;
this change does not reimplement its Apple or Tizen caller conversions.

~~ Respect runtime availability of XamlRoot for CPU DPI tracking ~~

The UWP minimum predates XamlRoot. Probe
ApiInformation.IsPropertyPresent("Windows.UI.Xaml.UIElement", "XamlRoot")
rather than selecting DPI handling solely at compile time. Use
XamlRoot.RasterizationScale when available and DisplayInformation.LogicalDpi
otherwise, with matching load/unload subscriptions. WinUI uses XamlRoot.
Update the bitmap brush scale when the fallback DPI changes, so bitmap
pixels and XAML layout stay aligned. This guard preserves the older-OS
path; the reported device execution was on Windows 11.

~~ Select the ANGLE interface explicitly for UWP rendering ~~

The UWP implementation reported an indirect-call-guard failure in
gr_glinterface_create_native_interface after background idle. Select
GRGlInterface.CreateAngle for the UWP SKSwapChainPanel instead of probing
the native GL interface first, matching its EGL context.

Keep WinUI's existing GRGlInterface.Create call in this change. The author
confirmed that the conditional deliberately limited the change to UWP.
Successful sample rendering demonstrates ANGLE bring-up, not a diagnosis
of the original CFG failure or proof of suspend/resume correctness.

~~ Share the ANGLE build while retaining the XAML-specific variants ~~

Extract the existing WinUI checkout and build steps into SyncAngle,
AngleGnArgs and BuildAngle in angle-shared.cake. Preserve revision-pinned
checkout, dependency synchronization, conventional import-library/PDB
names, the SkiaSharp GN config and the Windows SDK resource compiler.
Use the configured Visual Studio LLVM installation for Chromium's expected
clang-cl location; fail when that compiler is missing rather than selecting
another installation.

Mark .patch and .diff as -text so Git does not convert their line endings.

WinUI retains Windows App SDK/WebView2 preparation and its ANGLE variants.
UWP builds libEGL and libGLESv2 with target_os='winuwp' and
angle_is_winappsdk=false for the in-box XAML stack. Add x86, x64 and arm64
producer jobs, cache coverage and native-artifact merge inputs.

The pinned ANGLE chromium/8118 already derives ANGLE_ENABLE_WINDOWS_UWP
from the non-desktop WINAPI_FAMILY in platform.h, and its
IsWindowsVersionOrLater UWP branch bypasses VerifyVersionInfoW and
VerSetConditionMask. An unpatched winuwp/arm64 build succeeded, so this
integration does not carry custom replacements for those version helpers.

~~ Keep the Store CRT boundary while enabling native CFG ~~

UWP ANGLE initially linked desktop MSVCP140/VCRUNTIME140 imports while the
UWP native helper linked their _APP counterparts. The shared Spectre
/LIBPATH selected desktop CRT import libraries ahead of the Store paths.
Apply that library-path override only when current_os != "winuwp".
UWP then uses the Store CRT selected by its toolchain; the desktop WinUI
build keeps its existing Spectre library path.

The Store CRT does not supply the Spectre runtime-library variants, so
UWP artifacts are excluded from that PDB marker policy. This is separate
from Control Flow Guard: compile the UWP native helper with
ControlFlowGuard=Guard and link with ControlFlowGuard=true plus
/DEBUGTYPE:CV,FIXUP. Its x86, x64 and arm64 binaries were checked for
GUARD_CF and CF instrumentation. Reused Win32 Skia retains its own
static-CRT build contract.

~~ Use standard C++20 coroutine support with the v145 toolchain ~~

Build the new UWP native component with v145, matching the repository's
declared Visual Studio toolchain rather than requiring the older v143
platform-toolset registration.

On the CI MSVC 14.51 image, C++/WinRT's C++17 configuration added /await
and included experimental/coroutine, failing pch.cpp with STL1011.
Select stdcpp20 like the WinUI component. Merely disabling /await would
still leave the generated C++17 header path; C++20 selects the standard
coroutine header instead. Local /showIncludes verification found no
experimental coroutine header, and the three UWP native CI jobs pass at
d33acec5825. The helper implementations do not use coroutines.

~~ Pair CsWinRT versions with their SDK and signing contracts ~~

Use stable CsWinRT 2.3.1 and Windows SDK package 10.0.26100.87 for the
UWP Views and projection projects, with the UWP SDK values defined in
SkiaSharp.Build.props. Do not force that pair onto the existing WinUI
projection: retain its 19041 SDK package 10.0.19041.38 and update CsWinRT
from 2.0.4 to 2.1.6. The author reported the newer CsWinRT pair as
incompatible with the WinUI SDK selection.

Gate post-CsWinRT signing on SignAfterCsWinRTIIDOptimizer rather than
the presence of CsWinRTIncludes. WinUI opts in to signing after
CsWinRTReplaceForPatchedRuntime; UWP uses the normal CoreCompile signing
path. The UWP native project disables linker-generated Windows metadata,
and its packaged managed projection is distinct from WinUI's retained
WinMD outputs.

~~ Give UWP artifacts explicit native-test policies ~~

ArtifactCoverage rejected the new uwp outputs because they had no
inventory entries. Enumerate the UWP helper and ANGLE DLLs and PDBs for
x86, x64 and arm64, plus the architecture-neutral managed projection.
Assign their dependency, symbol and runtime-marker policies explicitly
instead of treating them as desktop artifacts.

Require VCRUNTIME140_APP.dll on native UWP DLLs and reject hard
VCRUNTIME/MSVCP imports that are not _APP variants. The managed projection
keeps the non-AppCrt policy; delay imports remain distinct. Accept its
portable PDB and verify its DLL CodeView identity and readable CLI metadata,
while native PDBs remain subject to the MSF identity checks.

The added CheckUwpDependencies build check examines the helper and managed
projection for desktop CRT prefixes. The artifact suite also checks ANGLE
and requires the Store runtime import on native UWP binaries.

The Native tests (Linux) check and the UWP helper/ANGLE producer checks
report success for CI build 1679151 at the current PR head. These assertions
inspect artifacts; they do not certify Store API usage or device lifecycle.

~~ Separate UWP and WinUI ARM64 API Scan surrogates ~~

Extend API Scan preparation with x64 package surrogates for the UWP ARM64
libEGL, libGLESv2 and native helper. Their ANGLE filenames overlap WinUI's,
so copy the UWP DLL/PDB pairs under surrogate-binaries/uwp and give the
UWP mappings that symbol location. Reuse the package-copy helper and fail
when a required surrogate file is absent.

Extend the preparation fixture to include UWP symbols packages and assert
the emitted mappings and copied surrogate set. This validates scan input
preparation, not an ARM64 runtime execution or a Store-certification pass.

~~ Keep the sample's MSBuild and deployment requirements explicit ~~

Add a packaged UWP sample with CPU, animated GPU and pointer-drawing pages,
including DPI-aware strokes, brush controls and Loaded/Unloaded animation
management. Provide self-contained publish profiles for win-x86, win-x64
and win-arm64 with PublishAot enabled.

Modern UWP XAML build/deployment requires Visual Studio 2026 MSBuild in
the documented workflow. Supply the project without a solution file so
the dotnet-based sample discovery does not attempt to build it; this is
not automated UWP sample coverage. Document the MSBuild command and
Visual Studio deployment that places the native assets in the package.
The in-repository sample imports both the core and UWP local-asset targets.
The UWP local target selects explicit Platform directories, but its AnyCPU
RID branches still match win10-* rather than the package's win-* RIDs.

~~ Use typed navigation results under NativeAOT ~~

The packaged AOT sample initially displayed blank page bodies. CsWinRT
returned the object-typed SelectedItem without the NavigationViewItem
runtime-class shape expected by the type test, so navigation never ran.
Read SelectedItemContainer as NavigationViewItemBase and dispatch from
its Tag instead. Explicit page types avoid relying on runtime discovery
of the object result.

The same package without this correction reproduced the blank pages.
Real-mouse validation exercised CPU drawing, GPU animation, page changes
and freehand drawing on x64 and x86/WOW64 packaged JIT and NativeAOT
layouts. ARM64 was build-validated, not run on hardware.

5320.title: [MAUI] Make SKGLView proxy window binding trim-safe
5320.body:
[MAUI] Make SKGLView proxy window binding trim-safe (#5320)

Fixes: https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/issues/5319

SKGLView bound ProxyWindowProperty to Window through MAUI's string-path
Binding constructor. That constructor is marked RequiresUnreferencedCodeAttribute
because string paths cannot be analyzed reliably by the trimmer, so constructing
SKGLView in a trimmed MAUI application emitted a warning.

Use BindingBase.Create with a static SKGLView expression for Window instead.
The binding retains source: this and is still assigned to ProxyWindowProperty,
while expressing the accessed property without a runtime string path.

The PR author reported no behavior change after applying the change to a .NET
11 MAUI project using SKGLView. CI's named managed-build and test jobs for
Windows, Linux, and macOS completed successfully; this does not assert that
every check passed, as the separate Windows native source benchmark job failed.

Co-authored-by: Benjamin Hall <bhall@ctr-electronics.com>

5809.title: [CI] Modernize Tahoe CI to Xcode 26.6 and .NET 10.0.404
5809.body:
[CI] Modernize Tahoe Apple toolchains (#5809)

Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1690550
Context: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1690908

Update the Apple CI images and toolchains while retaining the existing
target frameworks and deployment minimums. Image selection does not add
capacity to the public shared pool.

~~ Align Apple images and toolchains ~~

Select AcesShared Tahoe for public Apple jobs and hosted macos-26 for
internal package and test jobs. Update Xcode from 26.3 to 26.6 and the
.NET SDK from 10.0.403 to 10.0.404 across CI, global.json, containers and
integration-test defaults. Pair it with workload set 10.0.401; later Apple
workload sets require Xcode 27, which is not on the selected images.

Public build 1690908 passed 95 jobs at the preceding head 2d4f5c77931.
An internal iOS diagnostic captured an objc_msgSend cache-probe crash;
the source of the invalid pointer remains unknown.

~~ Provision tvOS in the jobs that require it ~~

The public Tahoe image lacked the tvOS platform needed by native tvOS
builds and the macOS sample build. Install the selected Xcode's default
tvOS platform in those public jobs after Xcode selection, with retries.
The native job skips installation on a cache hit. Internal jobs do not
receive this public-image provisioning step.

~~ Share Apple platform installation ~~

Replace install-ios-runtime.ps1 with install-apple-platform.ps1 for the
tvOS jobs and pinned iOS simulator runtimes. With a version, inspect the
runtime inventory, download if missing and verify availability afterward;
without one, install Xcode's default platform. Propagate command failures.

Normalize accepted platform names before calling Xcode or comparing
runtime names. PowerShell's ValidateSet accepts "ios", but the ordinal
inventory comparison expects "iOS"; without normalization, an installed
runtime could be reported missing. Local installer checks cover mixed-case
names, downloads, availability checks and failures.

~~ Stabilize the deadline-confirmation fixture ~~

Windows build 1690550 failed ScreenshotComparisonConfirmsFirstMismatchAfterDeadline:
the previous 2x2 capture was reported instead of the expected 4x4 image.
Prepare the confirmation image in the capture callback and allow its
completion source to run continuations inline. A local thread-pool
starvation reproduction produced the same failure with the forced
asynchronous handoff and passed without it; the precise hosted scheduling
delay was not traced.

Build 1690908 passed all 169 Windows Build sample tests, including the
deadline test. Its assertions, timeout and image tolerances are unchanged.

5827.title: Fix win-x64 crash on libjpeg/libpng longjmp error recovery
5827.body:
* Fix win-x64 crash on libjpeg/libpng longjmp error recovery (#5645)

Since 4.156 the Windows natives are built with the clang that ships with
VS 2026 (LLVM 22+). LLVM 22 pads some x64 calls with a nop for Windows EH
(llvm/llvm-project#144745), but CFGuardLongjmp's post-instruction label is
emitted after that nop, so the CFG long-jump table points one byte past the
real setjmp return address. Windows rejects the target and the process dies
(0xC0000005 with CET shadow stacks, 0xC0000409 without) whenever libjpeg or
libpng recovers from an error with longjmp.

The PDF backend hits this for every lazy non-JPEG image, because it first
offers the encoded bytes to the JPEG decoder. A malformed JPEG passed to
SKCodec.Create crashes the same way.

Link x64 clang builds with /guard:cf,nolongjmp. CFG stays enabled; only the
miscomputed long-jump table is dropped. arm64, x86 and MSVC builds are
unaffected and unchanged.

* Link the upstream LLVM issue from the nolongjmp workaround
5827.author: SimonCropp

5843.title: Fix SKRuntimeEffectUniforms starting with uninitialized memory; Reset() clears in place
5843.body:
The uniform block comes from sk_data_new_uninitialized, so a new
SKRuntimeEffectUniforms (and every Reset(), which allocated a fresh
uninitialized block) held leftover memory instead of the zeros Reset()
documents. Clear the block when it is created, and make Reset() clear it in
place: shaders, color filters and blenders copy it through ToData(), and
SkMesh::Make copies it (MakeWithCopy in sk_mesh.cpp), so nothing else holds it.
Reset() no longer allocates a native block and a wrapper per call.

Adds SKMeshUniformsBenchmark (a mesh rebuilt every frame with a reused
SKMeshBuilder) and tests for zeroed new/reset uniforms on effects and meshes.
ResetDisposesPreviousUniformBuffer becomes ResetKeepsAndClearsUniformBuffer:
there is no replaced buffer any more; it checks the same buffer is kept,
zeroed, and released on Dispose.


Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
5843.author: taublast

5679.title: Enable inset texture sampling and align Tizen blur configuration
5679.body:
Enable inset texture sampling and align Tizen blur configuration (#5679)

Context: https://skia-review.googlesource.com/c/skia/+/751778

Enable existing Skia rendering options at the native compilation boundary:
opt into inward texture-subset clamping and apply Tizen's CPU blur-path
selection to Skia itself rather than its wrapper.

~~ Keep filtered texture samples inside subset boundaries ~~

Bilinear filtering at the last pixel center of a texture subset can sample
the adjacent exterior row or column with a nominal weight of zero. Skia's
upstream "Add epsilon to texture effect clamping at pixel centers" change
adds an inward offset so filtering uses interior texels instead of
including undefined exterior data in the weighted sum.

Define SK_USE_SAFE_INSET_FOR_TEXTURE_SAMPLING in the Android, iOS, Linux,
macOS, Tizen, tvOS, WASM and Windows Skia GN recipes. At the pinned revision,
this changes Ganesh's linear inset from 0.5 to 0.5001 texels. It also rejects
the direct linear-copy path for identity-scale copies touching the logical
edge of an approximately sized texture, where backing storage extends
beyond that edge.

This enables existing Ganesh behavior, not a CPU or Graphite rendering
change. Texture-edge pixels may differ. Keep the definitions inline in the
platform recipes without changing shared build tooling or native APIs.

~~ Apply Tizen's blur selection when compiling Skia ~~

Tizen defined SK_AVOID_SLOW_RASTER_PIPELINE_BLURS in project_def.prop, which
compiles the wrapper and links the previously built Skia libraries. The
define therefore did not reach SkBlurEngine.cpp, where it selects the
CPU blur implementation.

Pass the define through Tizen's GN extra_cflags and remove the ineffective
wrapper definition. This bypasses the shader-based Gaussian candidate in
favor of the existing ThreeBoxApprox/Tent selection, matching the setting
in the other seven recipes. Blur pixels and performance may differ;
Tizen rendering and performance were not measured locally.

The macOS ARM64 native source build and complete net10.0 console test
solution passed at the final head: 6,613 passed, 48 existing skips and zero
failures. These checks do not establish pixel-identical rendering.

5145.title: [samples] Restore the Uno Gallery to the Windows solution (#3945)
5145.body:
PR #3835 removed SkiaSharpSample.Uno and the two SkiaSharp.Views.Uno
projects from SkiaSharpSample.Windows.slnx, because Uno.Resizetizer
crashed during the Windows Samples build:

  System.TypeInitializationException: ... SkiaSharp.SKColorSpace ...
  The version of the native libSkiaSharp library (116.0) is incompatible
  with this version of SkiaSharp. Supported versions of the native
  libSkiaSharp library are in the range [88.1, 89.0).

That no longer reproduces. Building the Uno sample directly on Windows,
from a clean obj/bin so UnoResizetizeImages actually runs rather than
being skipped as up to date:

  net10.0-desktop              build succeeded (52 PNGs + icon.ico generated)
  net10.0-windows10.0.26100    build succeeded
  net10.0-android              build succeeded

No TypeInitializationException and no native version error on any of
them. net10.0-browserwasm could not be completed locally, but for an
unrelated reason - the local Emscripten in the wasm-tools workload is
missing $(EmscriptenUpstreamBinPath) - and the Resizetizer had already
run successfully on that TFM before the link step failed. CI has a
working Emscripten, which is the remaining gap this change closes.

Note the underlying incompatibility has NOT been fixed upstream: every
published Uno.Resizetizer, including the latest 2.0.0-dev.2, still
bundles managed SkiaSharp 2.88.6.0, whose version gate only accepts a
native in [88.1, 89.0). Feeding that assembly a SkiaSharp 3.x native
still throws (verified in isolation with both 116.0 and 119.0). What
changed is that the Resizetizer task now resolves the matching 88.1
native it ships alongside itself, instead of a foreign one from the
build. So this is safe today but could regress if native resolution
around the Resizetizer changes again.

5293.title: [Testing] Add experimental image comparison APIs
5293.body:
[Testing] Add experimental image comparison APIs (#5293)

Add a separately packaged SkiaSharp.Testing library for comparing rendered
images, applying explicit acceptance policies and producing failure
diagnostics. Replace the copied test comparer and SkiaSharp.Extended dependency
while preserving existing golden-image acceptance behavior.

The implementation is managed-only and does not change native APIs, generated
bindings or rendering backends.

~~ Define image comparison and acceptance semantics ~~

Add SKImageComparison entry points for SKImage, SKBitmap and SKPixmap. Normalize
inputs to tightly packed BGRA8888 pixels, using exact unpremultiplied RGBA by
default and allowing callers to select premultiplied comparison where required.

Configure comparisons through SKComparisonOptions:

  * Per-channel absolute or percentage tolerances classify mismatched pixels;
    null disables a channel.
  * Tolerance masks widen enabled-channel allowances without changing raw error
    measurements.
  * Ignore masks remove complete pixels from errors, bounds and denominators;
    reject masks that leave no pixels to compare.
  * SKPixelMismatchBudget accepts inclusive pixel, percentage or combined
    limits. Percentage limits use exact decimal-rational arithmetic before
    flooring to whole pixels, avoiding floating-point boundary errors and long
    overflow.
  * Raw and thresholded metrics expose MAE, RMS and PSNR. Thresholded metrics
    exclude tolerated channels but retain the full magnitude of errors that
    exceed tolerance.
  * Mismatch, normalized MAE and normalized RMS gates combine with AND.
    Magnitude-only gates do not imply a zero-mismatch requirement.

Results are immutable managed objects and retain no native handles. Inputs and
masks are borrowed during each synchronous call; returned difference images are
independent caller-owned SKImage instances.

~~ Package and adopt the shared implementation ~~

Ship SkiaSharp.Testing as a signed package using the SkiaSharp family version,
currently 4.159.0. Register it with repository versioning, supported-package,
signing and solution infrastructure.

Mark the assembly experimental with SKIA4001 and record that diagnostic in the
experimental API registry. Consumers opt in through NoWarn or a pragma. An
internal ExperimentalAttribute compatibility type preserves metadata on targets
before .NET 8.

Remove the copied SKPixelComparer and SKPixelComparisonResult from
SkiaSharp.Tests.Shared. Route the shared Golden comparison boundary and SKTest
bitmap assertions through SKImageComparison while retaining their existing
golden lookup, retry, attachment, reference and tolerance policies.

Replace the SkiaSharp.Extended dependency in exact-package integration tests
with the matching SkiaSharp.Testing package. Remove the obsolete
PixelComparison.projitems import from the Samples project now that sample tests
use the shared golden harness.

~~ Add reusable difference diagnostics ~~

Add five opaque SKDifferenceStyle outputs using the same normalization,
tolerance and masking rules as comparison:

  * BinaryMask emits white mismatches on black.
  * ChannelDifference emits raw RGB differences.
  * ThresholdMap emits red mismatches, amber tolerated differences and gray
    ignored regions.
  * ThresholdOverlay, the default, blends classifications over the actual image
    after flattening transparency onto white.
  * Heatmap maps the largest raw enabled-channel difference onto a fixed
    blue-to-cyan-to-yellow-to-red scale.

Add an illustrated guide covering exact and tolerant comparison, mismatch and
magnitude gates, masks, alpha differences and diagnostics. Keep reusable inputs,
masks and outputs at 800x600, with separately named 850x650 checkerboard preview
images for documentation presentation.

~~ Cover compatibility and performance ~~

Add a dedicated SkiaSharp.Testing.Tests host covering acceptance, metrics,
normalization, masks, diagnostics, validation, ownership and each supported
input family. Register it with the .NET and Windows .NET Framework Cake test
runners, including x86 and x64 Framework jobs, and use Framework-compatible
enum enumeration.

Add BenchmarkDotNet coverage for image, bitmap and pixmap comparisons,
identical images, masks, diagnostics and mismatch-budget arithmetic across
representative image sizes. Include these workloads in source benchmark
tracking and preserve Release configuration through project references on clean
CI runners.

Cache normalized width during mismatch-bound calculation and skip channel
arithmetic for identical normalized pixels. On an Apple M3 Pro with .NET 10,
the measured 1920x1080 comparison improved from about 27.8 ms to 10.9 ms for
mostly identical pixels and from 54.7 ms to 28.8 ms for dense differences,
without materially changing managed allocations.

5743.title: [release] Document the dedicated SkiaSharp NuGet publisher
5743.body:
* [release] Document the dedicated SkiaSharp NuGet publisher

Replace retired MAUI publication instructions with pipeline 1715's Runs API contract, exact producer Build-number selection, live production resource verification, and signed shipping artifact boundary. Preserve ESRP approval and separate Finish consent, and document reporting rather than replaying failed or partial publications.

Update audit output and its existing regression checks so command-line guidance cannot route maintainers back to MAUI.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* [release] Tighten publisher guidance against production receipts

Consolidate the operator procedure and remove repeated guidance. Clarify producer run lookup, Azure parameter read-back, NuGet propagation and separate Finish authorization.

5784.title: Remove Linux x86 native build and packaging
5784.body:
Follow upstream .NET removal of linux-x86 cross-build infrastructure
(dotnet/runtime#136997, dotnet/runtime#137008, dotnet/arcade#17770,
dotnet/dotnet-buildtools-prereqs-docker#1821) by dropping the Linux x86
cross-compilation Dockerfile, CI jobs, native artifact checks, and
NuGet package entries.
